one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: I checked each verifier check's PASS and FAIL conditions against its expect line. Check 1 passes: its values ('00042', '  ab', 'xxx', '**7') all follow from left padding to width characters, with a space as the default fill. Check 2 passes: every case is s at or above width. Check 4 passes: exit status 0 is left as Advisory, which is looser than the words, not stricter. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition says every exported function "(this must include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft)" prints HAS-SECTION. The expect line only asks for a section for whatever functions index.js exports. It does not require capitalize, slugify or truncate to stay exported. A PR that dropped one of those exports and still documented every remaining export would meet the words but fail this PASS condition. That fixed list of names is a test the words don't force, so it belongs under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why: The files and tools the briefs name exist: index.js, README.md, test/strutil.test.js, and `npm test` mapping to `node --test`. The Check 1 and 2 node commands and `npm test` look sound. Check 3 breaks. It is a double-quoted bash string containing `new RegExp('\\b' + f + '\\b')`. Inside double quotes, bash turns `\\` into a single `\`. So node gets the JavaScript `'\b'`, which is a backspace character, not a regex word boundary. No README heading contains a backspace, so every exported function would print MISSING whatever the README says. The syntax is still valid, but the command does not do what the brief says it does: a quoting mistake makes it wrong when run as written. It would need `\\\\b` or single quotes around the outer string.

catches-traps.why:
I checked all three must_catch items against the briefs, and each one is handled.
1. Builder step 3 says README.md has "NOT for slugify" and tells the builder to "add a `## slugify(s)` section… as well as a `## padLeft(s, width, fill)` section".
2. Verifier Check 3 says "this must include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft". It FAILs if "any exported function prints MISSING or has no section", and it notes that slugify must now have a section.
3. Verifier Check 1 calls `p('ab',4)` with no fill argument and expects `"  ab"`, which confirms the default is space padding.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items against the verifier brief. Item 1: Check 3 loops over every exported function and prints MISSING for any that has no README heading. Its PASS says the list "must include capitalize, slugify, truncate and padLeft" and adds "slugify had no README section before this change; it must have one now". A README with a padLeft section but none for slugify therefore fails. Item 2: Check 1 uses only single-character fills and expects values that follow from line 1. Check 2's values ('abc',0 → 'abc') follow from line 2. Check 3 matches the function name in any markdown heading at any level, which is not a fixed layout. Check 4 needs only no failing tests. No check counts parameters or requires a one-character fill; the multi-character fill note is advisory. The builder's `## name(args)` format is a build instruction, not a PASS/FAIL condition.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks. The builder brief gives the same inputs and expected outputs that the verifier's Check 1 probe runs: "padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042', padLeft('ab', 4) === '  ab'". The verifier's script tests p('42',5,'0') and p('ab',4) and requires "00042" and "  ab". Step 4 repeats these as test cases ('42', 5, '0' -> '00042'; 'ab', 4 -> '  ab'). Step 5's "check by hand that every `export function` name in index.js appears as a README.md section heading" also restates Check 3's PASS condition (each exported name has a heading). The criterion lets the builder write its own tests. It does not let the builder brief carry a probe, meaning inputs with expected outputs, that also appears in the verifier brief. So the builder brief contains part of the checker's bar.
